clue.text: Metal peeler

definitions.meaning: old British slang for a police officer, after Sir Robert Peel who founded the Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Two words that seem to describe a metal kitchen gadget for skinning potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peeler' looks like a kitchen tool; it is a policeman, named after Robert Peel, the British politician who created the London police.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal Cu shares its name with British slang for a policeman, and a peeler is an older nickname for the same officer.

clue.text: This Parisian working later eats very small sausage

parts.note: French for 'this' is ce

indicators.note: eats means one piece takes the other inside it
working suggests the letters of the word later being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Parisian chef, busy later, tucks into a tiny sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges LATER to RELAT, and 'eats' puts V inside it after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervelat is a smoked pork sausage of European origin, here described as a small one.

clue.text: One type of exam recalled in school film

indicators.note: in means these pieces sit inside the other

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A school recalls an exam while showing a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns I plus ORAL into LAROI, and 'in' places that inside the school, here a group of whales rather than a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaroid is a brand of instant photographic film, so the trade name stands for the film itself.

clue.text: Pouring vessel that's more recent, but not new

indicators.note: but not tells us to drop the letter standing for new

parts.note: newer means more recent

explanation.surface: A jug is described as more modern, but somehow not new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes N from NEWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed jug once used for washing water, a vessel for pouring.

clue.text: Final appearance of pale lad in middle of Ramsgate

indicators.note: in means these pieces sit inside the other
middle of picks the central letters of the town's name

parts.note: wan means pale
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A pale young man makes a last appearance in the middle of a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the central two letters of Ramsgate, a seaside town in Kent, England; 'in' puts the pale lad between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan song is a farewell performance, from the legend that swans sing just before dying.

clue.text: British shopper obtains fresh Brie to make cheesy meal

parts.note: Welsh people are British

indicators.note: obtains means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rat is an informer, one who shops others to the police

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters of the cheese name being made anew in another order

explanation.surface: A British shopper buys some fresh Brie to cook a cheesy supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shopper' is not a buyer but an informer, someone who shops (betrays) people. 'fresh' rearranges the cheese to REBI, and 'obtains' holds it within the informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is melted cheese sauce on toast, a classic cheese-based snack or light meal.

clue.text: In the end, John associating with Yoko is something unacceptable

indicators.note: In the end means take only the final letter of the name John

parts.note: Yoko Ono, the artist who married John Lennon

explanation.surface: In the end, John Lennon's relationship with Yoko Ono was frowned upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' gives the last letter of JOHN; Yoko supplies her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-no is informal for a thing that must not be done, a taboo.

clue.text: Theatre event turning into a possibility

parts.note: an op, short for operation, is what happens in an operating theatre

indicators.note: turning means the letters of the word into are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A night at the theatre becomes a real possibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' is the operating theatre, not the stage. 'turning' rearranges INTO to TION.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is one of the choices open to you, a possibility you may take up.

clue.text: Setter maybe loose entering abbreviated definition of horse

indicators.note: entering means this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: gee-gee is a child's word for a horse, shortened to GG
to loose a knot is to undo it

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, perhaps, is let loose on a shortened definition of horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is the dog breed, not the crossword compiler. GG is short for gee-gee, a nursery word for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of dog trained to find game for hunters, one example of a gun dog.

clue.text: Stand absorbed by official example of sculpture

indicators.note: absorbed by means this piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: ref is short for referee, a match official
to lie means to remain or stand, as in 'let the matter lie'

explanation.surface: A sports official is absorbed by a stand featuring sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' is not a grandstand but the verb, as when a matter is left to stand or lie; 'absorbed by' puts it inside the official.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief is a carving that stands out from a flat background, a form of sculpture.

clue.text: Design keelboat, after vacation, being addicted to marine life

parts.note: a plan is a design

indicators.note: after vacation means the word keelboat is emptied, keeping only its outside letters

parts.note: on means hooked on or taking a drug

explanation.surface: Someone designs a keelboat after a holiday, having become hooked on sea creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a holiday; here it means emptying KEELBOAT to KT.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are tiny organisms drifting in seas and lakes, a mass of small sea life.

clue.text: Before pausing with round piece, grill bread

indicators.note: Before tells us the grill word comes first, before the pausing word

parts.note: to pump someone is to grill them with questions
er is the sound of a pause in speech
a nickel is a round coin, a five-cent piece

explanation.surface: Someone grills a round piece of bread after a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grill' is questioning, not cooking. A nickel is a US five-cent coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumpernickel is a dark, dense German rye loaf.

clue.text: Geezer regularly distributed a religious book

indicators.note: regularly distributed means taking every other letter of Geezer, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: An old man regularly hands out a religious book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly distributed' takes alternate letters of GEEZER: EZR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament, named after a Jewish scribe and priest.

clue.text: Forward returned up pitch

indicators.note: returned means the word up is read back to front

parts.note: to shy is to throw or pitch

explanation.surface: A forward came back up the football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' and 'pitch' suggest football; forward is the adjective for brash. 'returned' turns UP into PU.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward person is bold and presumptuous, which is what pushy means.

clue.text: Magic doctor US soldier heard

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: heard means we take the sound of the soldier's nickname, not its spelling

parts.note: GI Joe is slang for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A witch doctor's magic was overheard by an American soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magic doctor' reads as one phrase but splits: Magic is the definition, doctor gives MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mojo is a charm or magic power, originally in African-American folk belief.

clue.text: Means to absorb paintings etc back in Cornwall area

indicators.note: in means this piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: SW, the south-west of England, where Cornwall is

indicators.note: back means read the word in the opposite direction

parts.note: art covers paintings and similar works

explanation.surface: Paintings and other works return to a gallery in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ART into TRA. Cornwall is a county in the far south-west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw is a thin tube for sucking up a drink, a way to take liquid in.

clue.text: March winds essentially a beast

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration, or demo

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence, the centre letter of winds

explanation.surface: The March winds are, at heart, a wild beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' is a protest, not the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil spirit or monster, a fiendish creature.

clue.text: Greek writer and painter, having first time off work, terribly ashen

indicators.note: having first, with off, says the first of the time letters is taken away
off, with having first, signals that the letter for time is removed

parts.note: an artist may be a painter
op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of ashen are badly mixed up

explanation.surface: A Greek writer and a painter took time off work, looking terribly pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having first time off' drops the first T of ARTIST to leave ARIST; 'terribly' rearranges ASHEN to HANES.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristophanes was the great comic playwright of ancient Athens, author of The Frogs.

clue.text: French leader entertains circle, eating a biscuit

indicators.note: eating means taking in a further piece
entertains means holds inside, as a host holds guests

parts.note: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
the letter O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: The French president entertains his circle while eating a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' puts O into MACRON, and 'eating' then adds A after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a light almond or coconut biscuit, also spelt like the French macaron.

clue.text: Baltimoreans are here to ruin Dylan broadcast

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of Dylan are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Baltimore folk are here to sabotage a Bob Dylan broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges DYLAN to YLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore is the largest city of this US state, so its people live there.

clue.text: Hollywood actress's different aura near home

indicators.note: different means the letters of aura near home are made into something else

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star has a different aura when near home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges AURA NEAR HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish-born redhead starred in The Quiet Man and other classic Hollywood films.

clue.text: They're opposed to touching minute insect

indicators.note: touching means the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: antis are people opposed to something

explanation.surface: Some people object to handling a tiny insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' reads as tiny but gives M for the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying mantis is a predatory insect that holds its forelegs as if in prayer.

clue.text: British in charge follow sport's guiding rule

indicators.note: follow means the British and in-charge pieces come after the sport

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a sport

explanation.surface: British officials follow their sport's governing rule.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubric is a heading or instruction directing how something is to be done.

clue.text: Water emerging from seaquake

indicators.note: emerging from says the letters come out of the inside of seaquake

explanation.surface: Water surging up from an undersea earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emerging from' picks the letters out of seAQUAke.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is Latin for water and is used for it in English, as in aqua fortis.

clue.text: Search Computer World number

parts.note: to dig is to search, as in digging for information
IT, information technology, is the world of computers

explanation.surface: Someone searches a computer magazine for a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Computer World' looks like a magazine title but gives IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is any single numeral from nought to nine.

clue.text: Impressionable character that's crossed in street

indicators.note: in means this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: way is used in street names, like a road
the letter X is a character made of two crossing strokes

explanation.surface: An impressionable person is crossed in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressionable' means soft enough to take an impression, like wax.
explanation.definitionFit: Something waxy is soft and pliable, so it readily takes an impression.

clue.text: European prince outside in estate that's used to fence

indicators.note: outside means take only the outer letters of estate

explanation.surface: A European prince stands outside on his estate, which is fenced in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' means to sword-fight, not to enclose land.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is the sword with a stiff blade used in the sport of fencing.

clue.text: Succeeded cutting tax (grand)

indicators.note: cutting means this piece slices into the other

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, a UK sales tax
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in cutting tax by a grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like a thousand pounds; it means huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and vast both describe something imposing in its sheer scale.

clue.text: American highway staff attending diversion

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the two pieces sit together

parts.note: a turn is a change of direction, a diversion
a pike is a long staff with a spearhead

explanation.surface: Staff are attending to a diversion on an American highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but is a pole weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a turnpike is a toll expressway.

clue.text: Taken aback at fine commercial for aircraft

indicators.note: Taken aback means taken backwards, so the three pieces read in reverse

parts.note: OK means fine
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Someone is taken aback at a fine for advertising an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' looks like surprise but reverses AT OK AD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douglas DC-3 transport plane was named the Dakota in RAF service.

clue.text: Second tyre burst, with learner inside, behind closed doors

indicators.note: inside means this piece is placed within the other
burst means the letters of tyre are blown apart and rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: A second tyre bursts with a learner driver inside, and it is hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' rearranges TYRE into RETY; 'inside' puts L in it before the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Done behind closed doors is done in private, out of public view.

clue.text: Mick Jagger perhaps joins daughter on a trip

parts.note: Mick Jagger is singer of the Rolling Stones, so he is a Stone

explanation.surface: Mick Jagger takes his daughter on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' sounds like travel but means a drug experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a trip is drug slang for being high.
